title: Iteration-slope stability for a known physical corrector response
purpose: Separate fixed-point physics from affine iteration-slope policy in the simplest live MODFLOW system.

coupling_iteration.policy: At iteration k, evaluate exact q_swap(H_k), publish q_iter(H)=q_swap(H_k)+s*(H-H_k), solve the same MODFLOW time step from immutable H0, repeat.
coupling_iteration.note: This is a scalar Schur-complement/quasi-Newton oracle. The fixed point is independent of s whenever the iteration converges and A-s is nonsingular.

policies.name: POSITIVE_U
policies.expected: alternating divergence with error magnitude doubling while heads remain inside the one-cell domain for the fixed observation horizon

policies.name: SINGULAR_OVERLAP
policies.expected: A-s=0; no unique affine groundwater solve

gates: PHYSICAL_J reaches 8.01 m within 1e-10 m in the first live solve.
INTERCEPT_ONLY observed successive nonzero error ratios equal -0.5 within 1e-8.
POSITIVE_HALF alternates between equal-magnitude opposite-sign errors with ratio -1 within 1e-8.
POSITIVE_U observed error ratios equal -2 within 1e-8 for the fixed six-iteration horizon.
All nonsingular policies share the same analytically defined fixed point even though some do not converge to it.
SINGULAR_OVERLAP is recorded as nonconvergent or otherwise unable to certify a unique solve; no tolerance is changed.
interpretation_rules: s is an iteration-response slope, not automatically a physical coefficient.
Changing s can alter convergence without altering the physical fixed point.
A good iteration slope approximates the derivative relevant to the eliminated coupled residual; exact equality is sufficient for one-step convergence in this linear scalar case.
The singularity at s=A is an algebraic cancellation between groundwater Jacobian and published boundary response, not evidence of zero physical storage.
forbidden: do not infer that the scalar A or j values represent a real SWAP/MODFLOW field case
do not use convergence speed alone as evidence of physical correctness
